commands.title: Get-Help
commands.description: Shows the built-in manual page for any PowerShell command. Add -Examples to see ready-to-use samples. This is the fastest way to learn what a command does before running it.

commands.title: Get-Command
commands.description: Searches every command installed on your PC. Use it when you know roughly what you want (something with 'network' in the name) but not the exact command.

commands.title: Get-Process
commands.description: Lists running programs. This version sorts them by how much CPU time they have used and shows the top 10, so you can spot what is heavy on your PC.

commands.title: Stop-Process
commands.description: Force-closes a program by name. Anything unsaved in that program is lost, so close it normally first when possible.

commands.title: Get-Service
commands.description: Lists Windows services (background system components) and shows which ones are running. Reading is safe; it does not change anything.

commands.title: Restart-Service
commands.description: Stops and starts a Windows service. Commonly used to fix the print spooler. Anything that depends on the service is briefly interrupted.

commands.title: Get-ChildItem
commands.description: Lists files and folders in a location - PowerShell's version of 'dir'. Supports wildcards like *.log to find specific file types.

commands.title: Set-Location
commands.description: Changes the folder you are currently working in - PowerShell's version of 'cd'. The prompt updates to show the new location.

commands.title: Copy-Item
commands.description: Copies a file or whole folder to another location. Add -Recurse to copy a folder with everything inside it.

commands.title: Move-Item
commands.description: Moves a file or folder to a new location. The item no longer exists at the old location afterwards, unlike Copy-Item.

commands.title: Remove-Item
commands.description: Deletes a file or folder. Deleted items do not go to the Recycle Bin. Add -WhatIf first to preview exactly what would be deleted.

commands.title: Get-Content
commands.description: Shows the contents of a text file. With -Tail 50 it shows only the last 50 lines, which is ideal for watching the end of a log file.

commands.title: Get-ComputerInfo
commands.description: Shows a full inventory of your PC: Windows version, CPU, RAM, BIOS, network adapters, and more. A quick way to answer 'what exactly am I running?'.

commands.title: Get-Volume
commands.description: Lists your disk drives and partitions with their sizes and free space. Useful for checking whether a drive is nearly full.

commands.title: Test-Connection
commands.description: Checks whether your PC can reach another computer on the internet, and how long the round trip takes. The first tool for 'is my internet working?'.

commands.title: Get-NetIPAddress
commands.description: Shows the IP addresses assigned to your PC's network adapters. Handy when you need your local IP for file sharing or printer setup.

commands.title: Measure-Command
commands.description: Times how long a command takes to finish. Great for comparing 'before and after' performance when you tune something.

commands.title: Get-ExecutionPolicy
commands.description: Shows which script-running rules apply to your PC for each scope. Read this before wondering why a .ps1 script will not run.

commands.title: Get-Member
commands.description: Shows all the properties and methods an object has. Use it to discover what else you can read or do with whatever a command gives you.

commands.title: Where-Object / Select-Object
commands.command: Get-Process | Where-Object WorkingSet -gt 500MB | Select-Object Name, WorkingSet
commands.description: The two most useful pipeline commands: Where-Object filters items down, and Select-Object picks which columns to show. Together they turn a wall of output into a short answer.

commands.title: winget --version
commands.description: Shows which version of Windows Package Manager you have. Winget is the built-in Windows tool for installing and updating apps from the command line.

commands.title: winget search
commands.description: Searches the winget catalog for an app by name and shows the exact ID, version, and source you would need to install it.

commands.title: winget show
commands.description: Shows full details about an app before you install it: description, homepage, license, installer size, and the exact version that would be installed.

commands.title: winget install
commands.description: Downloads and installs an app from the winget catalog, found via 'winget search'. Add --silent to skip the installer's questions.

commands.title: winget uninstall
commands.description: Removes an installed app. Find the exact name or ID to use with 'winget list' first.

commands.title: winget upgrade
commands.description: Lists every installed app that has a newer version available. Running it with no app name changes nothing - it is a read-only check for updates.

commands.title: winget upgrade --all
commands.description: Updates every app that has an available update, one after another. This is the one-command way to keep all your software current.

commands.title: winget list
commands.description: Lists all the software winget can see on your PC, including apps installed outside the Store. Add a name to filter to one app.

commands.title: winget source list
commands.description: Shows which app catalogs winget searches (Microsoft's community repo, msstore, and any you added). Read-only.

commands.title: winget source update
commands.description: Refreshes winget's local copy of the app catalog so searches and upgrades see the latest versions. Fixes stale search results.

commands.title: winget info
commands.description: Shows winget's version, configuration, and which Windows version it is running on. Useful when troubleshooting winget itself.

commands.title: winget --help
commands.description: Shows the full list of winget commands and options with short descriptions. Add --help after any subcommand for its details.

commands.title: dir
commands.description: Lists the files and folders in the current folder. 'dir /s file.txt' searches all subfolders for a file.

commands.title: cd
commands.description: Changes the current folder. 'cd ..' goes up one level. 'cd' alone shows where you currently are.

commands.title: cls
commands.description: Clears everything from the Command Prompt window so you start with a clean screen. Nothing is deleted.

commands.title: copy
commands.description: Copies one or more files to another location. Use 'xcopy' or 'robocopy' for whole folder trees.

commands.title: move
commands.description: Moves a file to a new location. Unlike copy, the file no longer exists at the original spot afterwards.

commands.title: del
commands.description: Deletes files. Deleted files do not go to the Recycle Bin. Run 'del /p file.txt' to be asked for confirmation first.

commands.title: mkdir
commands.description: Creates a new folder inside the current one. Nested paths like mkdir A\B\C create all missing levels at once.

commands.title: rmdir
commands.description: Removes an empty folder. Add /s to remove a folder and everything inside it - double-check the path first.

commands.title: type
commands.description: Prints the contents of a text file to the screen. For very long files, 'more file.txt' shows it one page at a time.

commands.title: ipconfig
commands.description: Shows your PC's network configuration: IP address, subnet, and gateway for every adapter. The starting point for most network troubleshooting.

commands.title: ipconfig /flushdns
commands.description: Clears the cached list of website names and addresses. Fixes 'site works for everyone else but not me' problems after a DNS change.

commands.title: ping
commands.description: Sends four small packets to a server and reports whether they come back and how fast. The classic 'is the internet up?' test.

commands.title: tracert
commands.description: Shows each hop your traffic takes between your PC and a server, with timings. Reveals where a slow or broken connection actually is.

commands.title: netstat
commands.description: Lists active network connections and which program (by process ID) owns each one. Pair with 'tasklist' to match IDs to names.

commands.title: tasklist
commands.description: Lists all running programs with their memory use and process IDs (PIDs). The read-only companion to taskkill.

commands.title: taskkill
commands.description: Force-closes a program by image name or by PID (/PID 1234). Unsaved work in that program is lost. Add /F when it refuses to close.

commands.title: systeminfo
commands.description: Prints a detailed report about your PC: Windows version, install date, uptime, RAM, network cards, and pending hotfixes.

commands.title: whoami
commands.description: Shows the user account you are currently running as. 'whoami /priv' additionally lists your account's special rights.

commands.title: hostname
commands.description: Prints your PC's network name - the name other devices see when you share files or connect remotely.

commands.title: sfc /scannow
commands.description: System File Checker: scans Windows' own system files and automatically repairs any that are corrupted. Can take 10+ minutes.

commands.title: shutdown
commands.description: Restarts the PC immediately (/r = restart, /t 0 = no delay). Use /s to shut down, or /a to cancel a pending restart.

commands.title: set
commands.description: Lists all environment variables - the hidden settings every program reads, like PATH and TEMP. 'set PATH' filters to just one.

commands.title: where
commands.description: Shows the full path of a program that would run if you typed its name. Perfect for 'which version am I actually launching?' questions.

commands.title: tree
commands.description: Draws a visual map of folders and (with /F) files beneath the current folder. A quick way to see a project's structure.
